rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj transmits a third view that the referent is the Prophet Ṣāliḥ, who did not fear the consequences.
rows.anchor: والثالث أنه نبي الله صالح لم يخف عقباها حكاه الزجاج

none: سورة الليل is introduced by its recited verses only; no explanation is given in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two possible meanings of mā are the same as those explained at 91:5; male and female can mean Adam and Eve, or all males and females generally.
rows.anchor: وما خلق الذكر والأنثى في ما قولان وقد ذكرناهما عند قوله تعالى وما بناها

rows.speaker: ابن السائب ومقاتل
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies male and female as Adam and Eve.
rows.anchor: أحدهما آدم وحواء قاله ابن السائب ومقاتل

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the wording generally.
rows.anchor: والثاني أنه عام ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says that God undertakes to clarify the path of guidance and the path of error.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى إن علينا ان نبين طريق الهدى من طريق الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the present life and the afterlife belong to God, so let people seek them from Him.
rows.anchor: وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى أي فليطلبا منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire blazes and flares up.
rows.anchor: فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى أي توقد وتتوهج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched who enters this Fire is the polytheist.
rows.anchor: لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى يعني المشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person denied the Messenger and turned away from faith; al-ashqā here means al-shaqī, since Arabic uses the elative form for an active participle, as Ṭarafa's verse illustrates.
rows.anchor: الذي كذب الرسول ﴿ وتولى ﴾ عن الإيمان قال أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj rejects the Murjiʾa inference that only unbelievers enter Hell: this is one particular Fire, and Hell has ranks; otherwise 4:48 would have no point.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وهذه الآية التي من أجلها زعم أهل الإرجاء أنه لا يدخل النار إلا كافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver has no previous favor to repay; he did not act in return for a kindness shown to him.
rows.anchor: وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى أي لم يفعل ذلك مجازاة ليد أسديت إليه

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭāʾ says Abū Bakr bought Bilāl after his torture; polytheists claimed he was repaying a favor, and the revelation denied that.
rows.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس أن أبا بكر لما اشترى بلالا بعد أن كان يعذب قال المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives only to seek the reward of his Lord; al-Farrāʾ takes illā as “rather/only” and understands an omitted “his spending” before seeking.
rows.anchor: أي إلا طلبا لثواب ربه قال الفراء و إلا بمعنى لكن ونصب ابتغاء على إضمار إنفاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will be pleased with the reward given to him in Paradise.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى ولسوف يرضى أي بما يعطى في الجنة من الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following sūra was revealed after revelation had stopped for a period; three explanations are offered for the pause: the Prophet had promised answers about Dhū al-Qarnayn, the Cave Companions, and the Spirit without saying “God willing”; a companion's lack of cleanliness; or a puppy in his house.
rows.anchor: اتفق المفسرون على أن هذه [ السورة ] نزلت بعد انقطاع الوحي مدة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam specifically attributes the pause in revelation to a puppy in the Prophet's house.
rows.anchor: والثالث لأجل جرو كان في بيته قاله زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: جندب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report in al-Bukhārī and Muslim, a Qurashī woman taunted that the Prophet's devil had abandoned him, after which the opening verses of al-Ḍuḥā were revealed; she was Umm Jamīl, Abū Lahab's wife.
rows.anchor: وروى البخاري ومسلم في الصحيحين من حديث جندب قال قالت امرأة من قريش للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the afterlife is better for the Prophet than this world.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى قال عطاء خير لك من الدنيا

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another explanation says what the Prophet receives in the afterlife exceeds the honor bestowed on him in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره الذي لك في الآخرة أعظم مما أعطاك من كرامة الدنيا
